patch.value: Publish the canonical lifecycle policy contract every fleet repo enforces

pm-cli 2026.9.9 shipped a declarative lifecycle-policy engine (require_fields rules, advise/warn/refuse effects, an enforcement master switch). Measured on 2026-09-10 across all 23 fleet repos, every one returned policies:[] and enforcement:advise, so pm ops validate --check-completeness reported zero violations over 2,371 items: a gate that measures nothing, not a gate that passes. This publishes the canonical fleet policy set from pm-ops (the fleet's canonical-source package) so every consumer enforces the same contract via a thin launcher, not a vendored copy. The set covers evidence at terminal status for Issue, Feature, Task, Epic, Chore, Decision and Milestone plus the fleet rule that a closed item carries a resolution, all at effect:refuse under enforcement:refuse. A pure verify() reports drift (missing/extra policies, rule/effect/subject/description differences, enforcement below refuse), and a script wires it to release:check and CI.

lifecycle-policy.ts exports the canonical policy set as typed data with a description per policy explaining why; verify() is a pure function reporting drift over missing, extra, effect, rule, subject and description differences plus the enforcement level; scripts/verify-lifecycle-policy.ts shells out to the repo-pinned pm for pm schema policies --json, calls verify, prints a report, exits non-zero on drift, and uses the main-invocation runIfMain pattern; npm run verify:lifecycle-policy exists and is in the release:check chain; .github/workflows/ci.yml has an explicit verify-lifecycle-policy step and a pm ops validate --check-completeness --strict-exit step; pm-ops' own workspace has the canonical policies installed at enforcement:refuse; a non-vacuity test builds a throwaway workspace, installs the policies at refuse, asserts a violating close exits 4 with workflow_policy_refused, asserts a compliant close succeeds, and asserts verify detects a mutated policy effect; the revert-check (neuter verify) makes the drift test go red; coverage stays 100/100/100/100 and docstring coverage 100%; all gates green.

Every fleet repo can enforce one canonical lifecycle-policy contract exported from pm-ops; pm-ops itself runs under the contract it publishes with --check-completeness --strict-exit green; drift between an installed policy document and the canonical set is detected and reported.

Wired npm run verify:lifecycle-policy into release:check and CI. Installed the canonical policies into pm-ops at refuse. Backfilled 75 historical closed items the retroactive --check-completeness flagged.
